title: Private VPC Sales Cheatsheet — Regulated Buyers
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact salesperson/SE cheatsheet for conversations with regulated buyers evaluating Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Focus: explain the control plane model in plain legal/IT terms, pre-empt common objections, and provide quick technical signals to validate during discovery.

Audience:
- Enterprise risk/compliance officers
- Security/InfoSec architects
- Platform/Cloud architects evaluating private control planes
- Procurement and legal teams assessing contract redlines

Topline messages (30s elevator):
- We separate control plane and data plane: Redwood manages orchestration and UI (control plane) in a customer-isolated way while inference and customer data remain in your VPC or on-prem (data plane).
- Customers retain custody of keys, logs, and models. We never store customer unencrypted prompt text outside your environment unless explicitly configured.
- Designed to meet regulated workloads: audit trails, KMS/HSM integrations, network isolation, and policy-driven data residency.

Control plane mental model (plain language):
- What the control plane does: scheduling, deployment config, observability metadata, billing meter-reporting (optional), and rollout policies.
- What the control plane does NOT do: hold cleartext customer prompts, host production model inference, or access customer storage without explicit connectors.
- How we limit exposure: metadata-only heartbeats, encrypted config blobs, and a push-model for control commands (no inbound firewall openings required).

Key technical assurances to surface early:
- Key management: supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; we provide documentation for BYOK flows.
- No inbound tunnels: control plane communicates outbound to customer agents using mutual TLS and short-lived certs.
- Auditability: request/response hashes, token-level cost attribution exported to your log sinks, and configurable retention.
- Network posture: private endpoints (VPC peering, PrivateLink), egress controls, and optional air-gap deployment for on-prem.
- Data residency: model artifacts can be stored on customer-managed storage; logs and telemetry can be routed to customer SIEM.

Buyer objections + suggested responses (short scripts):
- Objection: "Your control plane will see our data."
  Response: "Our default production architecture keeps inference and customer data inside your VPC/on-prem. The control plane only handles encrypted configs and orchestration metadata. We also support BYOK and HSM so keys never exist in Redwood-managed KMS."

- Objection: "We need to audit every time an engineer touches a model."
  Response: "We provide role-based access logs and immutable audit trails exported to your SIEM; changes to model pinning, rollout, and config are recorded with user, timestamp, and commit diff."

- Objection: "What if the control plane goes down?"
  Response: "Inference continues to run in your data plane; the agent can catch & continue serving pinned models. Control plane downtime affects management actions, not runtime inference. We provide multi-region control plane options and documented failover procedures."

- Objection: "We need to understand vendor liability and contract redlines."
  Response: "We typically accept standard enterprise clauses but propose narrow limits on consequential damages and require joint scoping on data handling. Bring us your high-risk clauses early; legal can map them to technical mitigations (e.g., private deployments, dedicated capacity, or on-prem package)."

Discovery checklist for SEs (what to ask on first technical call):
- Deployment target: VPC (cloud + region) or fully on-prem?
- Network design: will you use VPC peering, PrivateLink, or direct connect? Any transit/proxy restrictions?
- Key management: do you require BYOK/HSM? Which provider (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, etc.)?
- Audit/log sinks: Splunk/Datadog/Elastic? Retention requirements?
- Models & artifacts: Will models be pulled from public registries, or do you need a local model registry/artifact store?
- Data sensitivity: PHI/PCI/FINRA? Any redaction or prompt-filtering requirements?
- Compliance regime: HIPAA, SOC2, FedRAMP, GDPR, or sector-specific regs?

Competitive positioning notes (concise):
- Against managed-cloud-only vendors: emphasize that we allow tenants to keep inference traffic and logs in their network while still offering a hosted control plane for operations — lower ops cost than fully self-hosted.
- Against self-hosted/runtime vendors: we provide a managed ops layer (control plane + expert support) and clear upgrade/rollback tooling; less engineering lift than building the orchestration layer in-house.
- Against large cloud provider AI endpoints: our differentiation is predictable unit economics and model-agnostic rollouts across hardware; we offer private deployment patterns that avoid vendor lock-in and proprietary runtime constraints.

Risk & mitigation mapping (short table in prose):
- Risk: leakage of sensitive prompts. Mitigation: keep all inference inside customer network, encryption in transit & at rest, BYOK, and optional local model storage.
- Risk: legal exposure for data processing. Mitigation: DPA with explicit processor/processor terms, scoping of data flows, and audit log exports.
- Risk: operational outages. Mitigation: pinned model serving in data plane, cached KV, and documented fallback policies.

Quick win signals to advance deal:
- Customer already uses customer-managed KMS.
- Platform team has an onboarding window for agents (1–2 weeks).
- Compliance lead requests a gap analysis — indicates interest in procurement.

Contract & procurement hacks (practical tips):
- Offer a joint technical statement of work (SOW) that maps redlines to technical controls—helps legal move faster.
- Use a short pilot SOW (30–60 days) limited to non-production traffic with a rollback clause; many regulated buyers accept this as a lower-risk starting point.

Sample email to compliance lead (short):
Hi <Name>,
Following our call, attaching a two-page technical summary that maps control plane behavior to your audit controls and KMS flows. If helpful we can schedule a 45-minute session with our security engineer to walk the network & key management diagram.
Best,
<Aisha>

Open questions / items for product/security to close before next sync:
- Provide an up-to-date architecture diagram specifically showing telemetry fields exposed to the control plane (itemize by key).
- Create a short BYOK integration runbook per cloud provider (AWS/Azure/GCP).
- Package a 30–60 day pilot checklist with clear exit criteria and data handling guarantees.

Notes: keep this doc short and shareable with sales + SEs. Turn recurring buyer questions into canned answers in the playbook repo and capture any legal redlines we frequently accept vs. escalate.
